title: Dangerous Evaluation and Deserialization knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best demonstrates understanding of “Dangerous Evaluation and Deserialization”?
options: Assume Ruby automatically guarantees every business rule and external system behavior.
Replace all built-in features with a third-party framework regardless of the task.
Skip tests because a short example ran once.
Use Dangerous Evaluation and Deserialization deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case.
questions.answer_key: Use Dangerous Evaluation and Deserialization deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case.
questions.explanation: Use Dangerous Evaluation and Deserialization deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case. The alternatives overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: When applying “Dangerous Evaluation and Deserialization”, which practice is the most reliable?

Treat all Ruby versions and third-party dependencies as identical.
Keep the dangerous evaluation and deserialization rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions.
Silence all errors and trust the result without inspecting inputs.
questions.answer_key: Keep the dangerous evaluation and deserialization rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions.
questions.explanation: Keep the dangerous evaluation and deserialization rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions. The alternatives overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unverified behavior.

Disable validation or security checks to make the example pass faster.
